semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Vision processing and image processing are often used interchangeably when describing techniques that involve the processing of visual information. They both deal with operations on images to enhance, analyze or modify them.

parent_domains.justification: Computer vision is a broader field that encompasses various techniques and processes related to processing and interpreting visual information from the world, of which vision processing is a subset.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Computer vision directly deals with the utilization of vision processing techniques to interpret and understand the visual world, hence closely related.

child_domains.justification: Image recognition is a specific task within vision processing that focuses on identifying objects or patterns within images.
Image segmentation is a precise operation under vision processing, involving dividing an image into parts for analysis.
Object detection is a task within vision processing that involves identifying instances of objects in images or videos.

closest_child_domain.justification: Image recognition is a foundational component of vision processing, directly dealing with tasks of interpreting visual data to identify objects.

sibling_domains.justification: 3D vision is a specific domain under computer vision concerned with processing three-dimensional visual information, similar to how vision processing might include processing various types of visual data.
Image analysis involves examining an image for understanding and extracting information, similar to the objectives of vision processing.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Image analysis closely aligns with vision processing in terms of intention, focusing on examining and making sense of visual inputs.

unrelated_domains.justification: While signal processing can involve processing of visual signals, it primarily deals with electronic signals more generally and is not strictly related to visual data.
Speech processing is concerned with the processing of audio signals to interpret and understand spoken language, which is distinct from vision processing.
Robot photography refers to the automation of capturing images using robots and doesn't strictly fit into the processing of visual data, which is the main focus of vision processing.
Like robot photography, robotic photography deals more with the capturing aspect rather than the processing of the captured visual data, hence different from vision processing.
